case_title: Sampath Kumar v. Inspector of Police, Krishnagiri
neutral_facts: The accused were prosecuted for the death of a man. There was no eyewitness to the incident. The prosecution claimed the deceased had a love affair with the sister of one of the accused, which was not approved by two of the accused. The trial court convicted all three accused based on the testimony of a witness who stated he saw the accused near the deceased and the presence of motive. The High Court upheld the conviction. The Supreme Court found the prosecution's case was based on circumstantial evidence and the witness's testimony was unreliable due to contradictions and lack of corroboration. The Court emphasized that motive alone is not sufficient for conviction and that the chain of evidence must be conclusive.
